news.headline: Vornado To Cash Out $575M In Stake Sale Of 90 Park Ave.
news.quote: Vornado is cashing out $575M from a 49% stake sale of the fully leased Class-A office tower in Midtown Manhattan.

touches.claim: Nine-month operating cash flow fell to 262,997 (table in thousands) from 1,112,112. Cash and cash equivalents fell to 580,496 from 840,850 at year-end, and revolver borrowings rose to 918,000 from 720,420. Investing, buybacks and debt service were funded partly by borrowing.

Leverage and financing risk are visible. Unsecured revolving credit facility borrowings were $918,000 at September 30, 2026, up from $720,420 at December 31, 2025 (table in thousands). Cash fell from $840,850 to $580,496 (table in thousands). Total liquidity was $1,911 (table in millions) against $2,397 at year-end 2025.

Growth is being financed with more debt and less cash: unsecured revolving credit facilities rose to 918,000 (table in thousands) from 720,420, and total liquidity was $1,911 (table in millions) at September 30, 2026. Interest expense, primarily from the 2033 senior unsecured notes, reduced the Q3 FFO bridge by 8.7. Growth therefore needs continued access to credit at manageable cost.
Vornado's core position is a large, Manhattan-centred office and street-retail portfolio. It owns 51 Manhattan operating properties, including 19.2 million square feet of office space in 26 of them.

news.why: Agreeing to sell a 49% stake in 90 Park Avenue at a $722.5 million valuation nets Vornado about $575 million in cash, substantially strengthening liquidity against its $580.5 million cash balance and $918 million revolver borrowings.
